You are the implementing engineer for Atlas ERP, in '/Users/taha/Claude projects/expremental ERP/atlas-erp' on branch feat/hr-time (dev merged; HR 10.1 employees/org + 10.2 leave done). NO git commands. uv at ~/.local/bin/uv; run `cd backend && ~/.local/bin/uv run <cmd>`. PostgreSQL 16 at postgresql+asyncpg://atlas:atlas@localhost:55432/atlas (LOCAL — run the full pg suite).

READ FIRST (binding): docs/research/s4hana-parity.md HCM (v1 = time tracking with project & cost-center allocation); docs/architecture.md D-012/D-013/D-014/D-015 (QuantityType for hours), D-022/D-025/D-007/D-029 (project id is an opaque PROJECTS-module id — but projects is Phase 11, NOT YET BUILT; cost-center id is an opaque finance id, validated). Then read:
- backend/app/modules/hr/ (extend): constants.py, models/ package, schemas.py, service/ package, queries.py (get_employee/employee_exists), router.py + sibling routers, the mounting.
- backend/app/modules/finance/queries.py (cost_center_exists — validate the time entry's cost center).
- The approval-flow pattern (leave request submit→approve from 10.2) as the timesheet template.
- backend/tests/modules/hr/{factories.py, conftest.py}.
Latest migration = 0038.

IMPORTANT — projects don't exist yet (Phase 11). A time entry can allocate to a PROJECT and/or a COST CENTER. Since the projects module isn't built, store project_id as a NULLABLE OPAQUE Uuid that is NOT validated against a projects table in v1 (document: project validation wires up when projects/queries exists in Phase 11 — for now project_id is a free opaque reference, cost_center_id IS validated via finance/queries). Do NOT create a forward dependency on projects. Phase 11 projects will add the validation + a queries hook; note this clearly in DECISIONS.

TASK — PLAN 10.3: time tracking with project & cost-center allocation. Build (extend hr):

1. hr/constants.py additions: TimesheetStatus (DRAFT|SUBMITTED|APPROVED|REJECTED) — a timesheet groups time entries for an employee over a period and goes through approval; or simpler: individual TimeEntry rows with their own status. DECIDE: a Timesheet header (employee + period) with TimeEntry lines is the cleaner SAP-like model AND supports approval at the timesheet level — use Timesheet + TimeEntry lines. Permissions hr.timesheet.read/.manage/.approve. Sequence 'hr.timesheet' (TS-…) optional.
2. hr/models additions (models/time.py; re-export):
   - `Timesheet` (`hr_timesheets`): UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, AuditMixin, TimestampMixin; (DocumentMixin if numbered) timesheet_number, employee_id (composite tenant_fk), period_start, period_end (Date), status (TimesheetStatus), total_hours (QuantityType — maintained sum of lines), submitted_at/approved_at (nullable), approved_by (nullable), notes. UNIQUE/index (tenant, employee_id, period_start).
   - `TimeEntry` (`hr_time_entries`): UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, TimestampMixin; timesheet_id (composite tenant_fk), entry_date (Date — within the timesheet period), hours (QuantityType — CHECK > 0), project_id (nullable OPAQUE Uuid — NOT validated in v1, the projects-module hook), cost_center_id (nullable OPAQUE finance cost-center id — VALIDATED via finance/queries), task_description (str), is_billable (bool default false). UNIQUE(tenant, timesheet_id, ...)? entries can repeat per day/project; just index (tenant, timesheet_id). 
3. hr/schemas additions: Create/Update/Read/Filter for Timesheet (+ entries as nested or sub-resource), TimeEntry; action payloads SubmitTimesheet, ApproveTimesheet/RejectTimesheet.
4. hr/service additions (service/timesheets.py + reads if >400): 
   - create_timesheet (DRAFT, employee exists, period valid end>=start, claim TS number), add/update/remove time entries (DRAFT only; entry_date within period, hours > 0, cost_center exists if set, project_id stored as-is; maintain total_hours), submit (DRAFT→SUBMITTED), approve (SUBMITTED→APPROVED, permission hr.timesheet.approve), reject, cancel. Idempotency on create/submit/approve.
   - allocation reporting: `hours_by_cost_center(tenant, period)` / `hours_by_project(...)` — set-based aggregates over APPROVED time entries (the cost/project allocation deliverable; useful for project costing in Phase 11 and CO reporting).
5. hr/queries additions: get_timesheet, timesheets_for_employee, approved_hours_for_project(project_id) (Phase 11 projects will call this for project cost/time), approved_hours_for_cost_center. The only imported file.
6. hr/router additions (timesheet_router sibling, mounted): timesheets (CRUD + nested time-entries GET/POST/DELETE + submit/approve/reject/cancel; list paginated, filter employee/status/period), an allocation report endpoint GET /timesheets/allocation?by=cost_center|project&from=&to=. Permission-guard (manage vs approve). PERFORMANCE §6. Mount.
7. NO cross-module events (time is intra-HR; payroll 10.4 + project costing 11 will READ approved time via queries). No events.py.
8. Migration 0039_hr_time.py (down_revision 0038): hr_timesheets + hr_time_entries + indexes. No trigger-bearing alters.
9. docs/modules/hr.md: add a Time Tracking section (timesheet + entries, project/cost-center allocation, the project_id-is-opaque-until-Phase-11 note, the approval flow, allocation reports). DECISIONS.md D-054 (timesheet+entry model with approval; project_id opaque/unvalidated until projects module exists, cost_center validated; allocation aggregates over approved entries feed project costing + CO).
10. Tests: test_timesheets.py (create + entries, entry-date-in-period, hours>0, cost-center existence, project_id-stored-opaque, total_hours maintained, submit/approve/reject lifecycle, RBAC manage vs approve), test_time_allocation.py (hours_by_cost_center / by_project aggregates over approved entries), test_time_api.py (endpoints + RBAC + pagination + ≤3 budgets + tenant isolation + the allocation report). 

RULES: no TODO/stub/dead-file; absolute imports; ruff + pytest FULLY green SQLite (`-m "not pg and not perf"`) AND `-m pg` (reset pg schema, alembic upgrade head, run -m pg); delete stray atlas.db; every file <400 lines; comments only non-obvious; don't print file contents. Update PROGRESS.md + tick PLAN 10.3 + DECISIONS.md D-054. Run STRUCTURE §9 self-check and report it.

Return: files created/changed, the timesheet/entry model + approval, the project_id-opaque-until-Phase-11 decision + cost-center validation, the allocation aggregates, test counts (SQLite total+new, pg), migration number, §9 self-check, deviations.

1	# SAP S/4HANA → Atlas Parity Map
2	
3	This document benchmarks Atlas ERP against SAP S/4HANA, the de-facto reference for enterprise ERP scope. Its purpose is twofold: to define what "complete" means for each functional area by enumerating the capabilities practitioners consider essential in current S/4HANA (2025/2026 releases), and to record — capability by capability — what Atlas v1 implements in full, what it implements in reduced form, and what it deliberately leaves out. The Atlas v1 scope is derived directly from this benchmark: every cut is documented with its rationale and an intended later path, so the gaps are commitments, not omissions. Research for this map was conducted in June 2026.
4	
5	**Methodology.** All twelve functional areas below were verified through live web research against current sources (SAP Help Portal, SAP Learning, SAP Community, SAP PRESS, and ERP consulting publications); no area was built from the embedded knowledge baseline alone. Five areas — Financial Accounting, Inventory Management & Warehousing, Quality Management & Plant Maintenance, Project System, and Cross-cutting platform concepts — supplemented web findings with embedded S/4HANA knowledge for specific subtopics or where source pages could not be fetched; these are flagged in the Sources appendix.
6	
7	Reading the tables: capabilities that practitioners consider **essential** are shown in bold. The Notes column preserves, verbatim, the scoping rationale and the planned later path for every partial and out-of-scope capability — that record is the contract of this document.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## Mandatory design inheritances
12	
13	Two S/4HANA architectural principles are hardcoded into Atlas and are non-negotiable across all modules:
14	
15	1. **Universal Journal pattern.** Atlas maintains one append-only financial line-item table as the single source of truth for all accounting data — the analogue of S/4HANA's ACDOCA. Every FI and CO view (trial balance, cost center report, margin analysis, financial statements) is a projection over this table. Totals are never separately stored; there are no aggregate tables to reconcile, and FI/CO reconciliation is eliminated by construction.
16	
17	2. **Document flow.** Every business document in Atlas records its predecessor and successor links (quote → order → delivery → invoice → journal entry, requisition → PO → goods receipt → supplier invoice, and so on), and the UI can render the full chain from any document in either direction — the analogue of S/4HANA's document flow and Document Relationship Browser.
18	
19	---
20	
21	## Summary
22	
23	| S/4HANA area | Full | Partial | Out of scope | Total |
24	|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
25	| Financial Accounting (FI) | 5 | 5 | 2 | 12 |
26	| Controlling (CO) | 4 | 4 | 3 | 11 |
27	| Procurement (MM-PUR) | 6 | 3 | 3 | 12 |
28	| Inventory Management & Warehousing (MM-IM / EWM) | 5 | 3 | 3 | 11 |
29	| Sales & Distribution (SD) | 2 | 6 | 4 | 12 |
30	| Production Planning (PP) | 4 | 3 | 5 | 12 |
31	| Quality Management & Plant Maintenance (QM / PM-EAM) | 1 | 4 | 7 | 12 |
32	| Human Capital Management (HCM / SuccessFactors) | 5 | 5 | 2 | 12 |
33	| Project System (PS) | 2 | 2 | 8 | 12 |
34	| Cross-cutting platform concepts | 5 | 3 | 3 | 11 |
35	| Fiori UX & Embedded Analytics | 3 | 6 | 3 | 12 |
36	| Industry Solutions approach | 3 | 4 | 3 | 10 |
37	| **Total** | **45** | **48** | **46** | **139** |
38	
39	---
40	
41	## Financial Accounting (FI)
42	
43	SAP S/4HANA Financial Accounting centers on the Universal Journal (table ACDOCA), which merges general ledger, controlling, asset, and material-ledger line items into one multi-dimensional single source of truth, eliminating FI/CO reconciliation. Around that core sit Accounts Payable (vendor invoices, automatic payment runs), Accounts Receivable (customer invoices, dunning, incoming payments), Asset Accounting (ledger-based parallel valuation and depreciation), Bank and Cash Management, tax determination via tax codes and procedures, real-time financial statements drawn directly from the journal, and orchestrated period-end/year-end close. Distinctive S/4HANA traits practitioners flag as essential include parallel ledgers for multi-GAAP accounting, document splitting for dimension-complete balance sheets, up to 10 parallel currencies, and posting-period control.
44	
45	| S/4HANA capability | Atlas v1 | Atlas module | Notes |
46	|---|---|---|---|
47	| **General Ledger on the Universal Journal (ACDOCA)** | Full | finance | — |
48	| **Chart of accounts and fiscal year / posting period control** | Full | finance | — |
49	| **Multi-currency accounting and foreign currency valuation** | Partial | finance | Atlas v1 (PLAN 4.3 done) has transaction + functional currency, a rates table (SPOT/CLOSING, direct-or-inverse lookup), posting-time translation with frozen functional amounts (largest-remainder residual balancing), purpose-keyed FX posting defaults, and an **unrealized**-FX revaluation run with auto-reversal. **Bounded out of v1:** group/additional parallel currencies; consolidation-style translation; **realized** FX (deferred to AP/AR clearing — purposes wired now); and **per-open-item** revaluation granularity — v1 revalues the per-account monetary foreign balance (accounts flagged `is_monetary` with a foreign `currency_code`), not individual uncleared AP/AR items. Later: add per-line extra currency columns + open-item-granular revaluation + realized FX at clearing, reusing the same rates-table and FX-account machinery. |
50	| **Accounts Payable (vendor invoices, payment runs, aging)** | Full | finance | Core AP (vendor bills, payment runs, aging) is planned; bank payment file formats (ISO 20022/NACHA) and withholding tax are not explicitly in v1. Later: Layer payment-media file generation and withholding tax codes onto the existing payment-run engine. |
51	| **Accounts Receivable (customer invoices, receipts, dunning, aging)** | Full | finance | — |
52	| **Asset Accounting (parallel valuation, full lifecycle)** | Partial | finance | Atlas v1 is "asset accounting lite": register plus straight-line and declining-balance depreciation runs posting journals; no parallel depreciation areas, transfers, retirements with gain/loss, revaluation, or assets under construction. Later: Extend the asset register with lifecycle events (transfer/retire/AuC settle) and per-ledger depreciation areas reusing the existing depreciation-run poster. |
53	| **Bank and Cash Management** | Partial | finance | Atlas v1 covers bank reconciliation via CSV statement import with match suggestions only; no standard bank formats (MT940/CAMT), no auto-clearing rules engine, no cash positioning or liquidity forecasting. Later: Add MT940/CAMT.053 parsers feeding the same import pipeline, then a cash-position report over bank-clearing accounts. |
54	| **Tax handling (tax codes, determination, compliance reporting)** | Partial | finance | Atlas v1 plans line-level configurable tax codes (rate, jurisdiction, inclusive/exclusive) — the calculation core — but no withholding tax, no statutory tax return reports, and no external tax engine integration. Later: Build tax-return reports as queries over tax-coded journal lines and add a pluggable external tax-calculation interface. |
55	| **Financial statements and real-time reporting** | Full | finance | — |
56	| **Period-end and year-end close** | Partial | finance | Atlas v1 has the enforcement primitives (period open/close at service and DB level, FX revaluation accounts, depreciation runs) but no year-end balance carryforward, accrual engine, GR/IR regrouping, or close task orchestration. Later: Add a balance-carryforward job and a simple checklist-style close task list on top of existing period states. |

181	| **Measurement points and counters** | Out of scope | — | Explicitly excluded from the v1 list; no condition readings or counter-driven triggers are planned. Later: Add a measuring point entity on equipment with reading documents that feed maintenance plan scheduling. |
182	| **Maintenance task lists** | Out of scope | — | Not in the v1 plan; v1 preventive/corrective orders would carry free-text work instead of reusable standardized operations. Later: Add a task list master assignable to maintenance plan items and copyable into orders. |

184	---
185	
186	## Human Capital Management (HCM / SuccessFactors)
187	
188	In current S/4HANA, HR is delivered as "SAP HCM for SAP S/4HANA" (H4S4) — switched on by default from the S/4HANA 2025 release, with the old HCM compatibility pack retired — while SAP's strategic, go-forward HCM is the SuccessFactors cloud suite (Employee Central, EC Payroll, Time Tracking, Recruiting, Onboarding, Learning, Performance, Compensation, Succession). H4S4 carries forward essentially the full SAP ERP HCM scope: Personnel Administration, Organizational Management, Time Management (work schedules, time evaluation, CATS timesheet with cost-center/WBS allocation), localized gross-to-net Payroll with retro calculation and posting to FI/CO, plus ESS/MSS, benefits, compensation and some talent functions. Atlas v1's plan covers the org, employee-master and leave cores well, covers timesheet capture and payroll-to-GL in reduced form, and deliberately leaves out talent, recruiting, benefits and jurisdiction-compliant payroll — the main honest gaps versus what HR practitioners consider a complete HCM suite.
189	
190	| S/4HANA capability | Atlas v1 | Atlas module | Notes |
191	|---|---|---|---|
192	| **Employee master data (Personnel Administration)** | Full | hr | **Done (PLAN 10.1, D-052):** `hr_employees` (`Employee`) — user-coded employee master with department/position/manager/optional-login links and MASKED compensation/PII (`base_salary`, `national_id`, `tax_id`, `date_of_birth`, `bank_account` behind `hr.employee.read_compensation` via the D-009 `Masked` serializer; written only at create + the dedicated `PATCH /employees/{id}/compensation`). Later: Add date-effective history and formal hire/transfer/terminate actions on the existing employee entity. |
193	| **Organizational management (org units, positions, org chart)** | Full | hr | **Done (PLAN 10.1, D-052):** `hr_departments` (`Department`, self-FK hierarchy + cost-centre link + soft manager link) + `hr_positions` (`Position`) + the reporting ORG CHART (`Employee.manager_id` self-FK; `GET /employees/org-chart`, bounded recursive build). Department hierarchy and manager reporting line are both cycle-guarded. Later: Extend later with date-effective org structures and job catalogs if needed. |
194	| **Leave and absence management** | Full | hr | Later: Later add collision checks with work schedules and quota carryover rules. |
195	| **Time recording with account assignment (CATS-style timesheet)** | Full | hr | Later: Planned core (capture + project/cost-center allocation) matches CATS; approval/transfer-to-costing flows can be hardened later. |
196	| **Time evaluation and work schedules** | Partial | hr | Atlas v1 plans timesheet capture and leave only; no work-schedule rules, shift planning or rule-based evaluation of overtime/premiums. Later: Add work-schedule calendars and a rules-based time evaluation step that feeds payroll inputs. |
197	| **Payroll (localized gross-to-net with retro calculation)** | Partial | hr | Atlas v1 plans only a simple gross-to-net calculation explicitly flagged as not jurisdiction-compliant; no country legal rules, retro accounting, payment files or statutory reporting. Later: Integrate certified third-party/localized payroll engines via connector, or ship country compliance packs incrementally. |
198	| **Payroll posting to finance (FI/CO integration)** | Full | hr | Later: Later refine with configurable wage-type-to-account mapping and accrual postings. |
199	| **Employee and manager self-service (ESS/MSS)** | Partial | hr | Leave approvals and time entry imply basic self-service, but no planned employee self-service for personal data, payslips, or manager team dashboards. Later: Add ESS/MSS screens on top of existing HR APIs in the frontend once core records and payroll outputs exist. |
200	| **Compensation management (pay structures and review cycles)** | Partial | hr | **Partial (PLAN 10.1, D-052):** Atlas v1 stores only static MASKED compensation fields on the employee (`base_salary` + `currency_code`, gated by `hr.employee.read_compensation`, written via the dedicated compensation endpoint); no pay-grade structures or compensation review cycles. Later: Add pay-grade/salary-band tables and a periodic comp review workflow over the masked fields. |
201	| **Talent management (recruiting, onboarding, learning, performance, succession)** | Out of scope | — | Explicitly excluded from the v1 list; v1 targets core HR/time/payroll-lite, and even SAP treats talent as a separate cloud suite rather than ERP core. Later: Add as a separate talent module or integrate an open-source ATS/LMS against the employee and org APIs. |
202	| **Benefits administration** | Out of scope | — | Explicitly excluded from v1; meaningful benefits administration depends on compliant payroll deductions, which v1 also lacks. Later: Add plan/eligibility/enrollment objects feeding deduction lines once payroll gains real deduction handling. |
203	| **HR reporting and analytics** | Partial | reporting | v1 plan includes the org chart and operational record views but no HR KPI analytics (headcount trends, absence rates, labor cost). Later: Build headcount/absence/labor-cost reports on the shared reporting module over HR and journal data. |
204	
205	---
206	
207	## Project System (PS)
208	
209	S/4HANA Project System manages internal, capital-investment, and customer projects through hierarchical work breakdown structures (WBS) and optional networks/activities, covering structure planning, scheduling, cost and revenue planning, budgeting with availability control, execution postings (time via CATS, procurement, goods movements), and period-end close via settlement and results analysis / event-based revenue recognition. In current S/4HANA (2025/2026) the area spans classic PS (on-premise/private cloud) and the Fiori-based Enterprise Projects and Professional Services Projects in Enterprise Portfolio and Project Management (public cloud). The Atlas v1 plan (WBS as costing objects, time and purchases postable to WBS, a project cost report) covers the execution-side core — structures and actual-cost collection — but deliberately omits the planning and financial-close layers: networks/scheduling, cost planning, budgeting/availability control, settlement, results analysis/revenue recognition, and customer-project billing are all out of scope for v1.
210	
211	| S/4HANA capability | Atlas v1 | Atlas module | Notes |
212	|---|---|---|---|
213	| **Project definitions and WBS structures** | Full | projects | Later: Templates, status management, and mass-change tooling can be layered on the same WBS entity later. |
214	| **Networks, activities, and relationships** | Out of scope | — | Atlas v1 explicitly excludes networks; the v1 model is WBS-only cost collection with no activity/task layer. Later: Add an activity entity under WBS elements with relationships and confirmations, then attach scheduling and material components. |
215	| **Project scheduling and milestones** | Out of scope | — | Scheduling is explicitly not in the v1 list and depends on the network/activity layer, which is also excluded. Later: Introduce basic/forecast dates on WBS and activities plus a scheduling engine and Gantt view once networks exist. |
216	| **Project cost planning** | Out of scope | — | Atlas v1 collects only actual costs on WBS; no plan versions or planned-cost entry are in the plan, so the cost report has no plan/actual comparison. Later: Add a plan-cost table keyed by WBS element and period, then extend the project cost report to plan-vs-actual. |
217	| **Project budgeting and availability control** | Out of scope | — | Budgeting controls are explicitly excluded from the v1 list; v1 has no budget object and no posting-time funds check. Later: Add a budget amount per WBS with tolerance rules evaluated in the posting pipeline before actuals commit. |
218	| **Time recording to projects (CATS-style)** | Full | projects | Later: Approval workflows and posting to network activities can follow once those features exist. |
219	| **Procurement and expense postings to projects** | Partial | projects | Atlas v1 plans actual purchase and expense postings to WBS, but PR/PO commitment tracking and project stock / project MRP are not planned. Later: Derive commitment records from open purchase orders assigned to WBS, then add project-stock segments in inventory. |
220	| **Project settlement** | Out of scope | — | Settlement is explicitly excluded from v1; collected costs remain on the WBS with no period-end transfer to receivers. Later: Add settlement rules per WBS and a periodic settlement run reusing the finance allocation/posting engine. |
221	| **Results analysis / event-based revenue recognition** | Out of scope | — | No revenue recognition or WIP/POC valuation of project costs is planned in v1; v1 projects are pure cost collectors. Later: Implement event-based recognition postings in the finance module triggered by project cost and billing events. |
222	| **Customer project billing integration** | Out of scope | — | Not in the v1 list; there is no planned sales-order-to-WBS link or billing generated from project time/expenses. Later: Link sales order lines to WBS elements, then generate resource-related billing proposals from posted time and expenses. |
223	| **Project cost reporting and analytics** | Partial | projects | v1 plans a project cost report over actuals by WBS, but without plan or commitment columns and without the broader drilldown/overview suite, it is a reduced subset. Later: Extend the report with commitment and plan columns and line-item drilldown as those data objects are added. |
224	| Progress analysis / earned value management | Out of scope | — | Depends on cost planning, budgets, and scheduling, none of which are in v1; also not considered core by most practitioners outside EPC/engineering industries. Later: Compute POC and earned value from plan-cost and confirmation data once planning and scheduling layers exist. |
225	
226	---
227	
228	## Cross-cutting platform concepts
229	
230	Cross-cutting platform concepts in S/4HANA (2025/2026) are the architectural primitives every functional module relies on: the Universal Journal (ACDOCA) as the single financial line-item table; document flow with predecessor/successor links viewable in the Document Relationship Browser; the mandatory unified Business Partner model (CVI-synchronized customer/vendor views); the BRF+/Adobe Forms output management framework; configurable number ranges per document type; the roles/profiles authorization concept (PFCG on-premise, business roles with restrictions in Cloud); and the client (MANDT) field on nearly every table on-premise, replaced by tenant isolation in S/4HANA Cloud SaaS. Atlas v1 deliberately inherits the two load-bearing patterns (Universal Journal, document flow) and covers tenancy, RBAC, audit, and numbering, while consciously deviating on the Business Partner model and deferring output management, workflow, and extensibility.
231	
232	| S/4HANA capability | Atlas v1 | Atlas module | Notes |
233	|---|---|---|---|
234	| **Universal Journal (ACDOCA) as single source of truth** | Full | finance | — |
235	| **Document flow / Document Relationship Browser** | Full | core | — |
236	| **Unified Business Partner model (BP + CVI)** | Partial | core | Deliberate deviation: Atlas v1 keeps separate vendor and customer master tables; customer/vendor master data itself is planned, but there is no unified party object, no shared roles/relationships, and no single identity for an entity that is both customer and supplier. Later: Introduce a thin party/business-partner table that links existing customer and vendor records as roles, without restructuring the two masters. |
237	| **Output management (determination rules, channels, form templates)** | Partial | core | Atlas v1 plans only basic document rendering; the rule-based determination framework, multi-channel dispatch (email/EDI), template management, and output status/retry queue are explicitly not in the v1 list. Later: Add a rule-driven output determination service (document attributes → channel + template + recipient) with pluggable channel adapters and a retryable output queue. |
238	| **Number ranges (document numbering)** | Full | core | Later: Add external number assignment and per-fiscal-year ranges later if conversion/legal scenarios demand them. |
239	| **Authorization concept (roles, profiles, restrictions)** | Partial | admin | Atlas v1 plans the RBAC core (JWT auth, roles → permissions → resources stored as data), but S/4HANA's field/org-value restrictions (scoping a permission to specific company codes, plants, etc.) and segregation-of-duties analysis are not in the v1 list. Later: Extend permission records with attribute/scope filters (org-unit values) evaluated alongside the tenant filter, then layer SoD rule checks on role assignments. |
240	| **Multi-client architecture / SaaS multi-tenancy** | Full | core | — |
241	| **Audit trail / change documents** | Full | core | Later: Add read-access logging for sensitive fields as a later compliance increment. |
242	| **Extensibility framework (custom fields, key-user and side-by-side extensions)** | Out of scope | — | No custom-field or extension mechanism appears anywhere in the Atlas v1 plan; v1 ships fixed schemas only. Later: Add JSONB custom-field columns with metadata-driven validation on core entities, plus webhook/event hooks per document type. |
243	| **Workflow engine (flexible approval workflows)** | Out of scope | — | No approval/workflow capability is in the Atlas v1 plan; documents post directly without configurable release strategies, which practitioners consider a core control in procurement and finance. Later: Add a generic approval service (document type + condition → ordered approver steps) driving a status field that blocks posting until approved. |
244	| **Released APIs and event-based integration** | Out of scope | — | The Atlas v1 cross-cutting scope defines internal patterns (journal, flow, tenancy, auth) but lists no public API contract or event emission for external integration. Later: Publish the existing internal REST endpoints as a versioned public API and emit domain events (document created/changed) to a message bus or webhooks. |

246	---
247	
248	## Fiori UX & Embedded Analytics
249	
250	In current S/4HANA (2025/2026), this area covers the Fiori design system (Horizon theme, SAPUI5/Fiori elements controls), the role-based launchpad organized into spaces and pages with app/KPI/insight tiles, standard floorplans (list report, object page, overview page, analytical list page, worklist), and embedded analytics built on the CDS virtual data model: analytical queries, Smart Business KPI tiles with thresholds and drill-down, multidimensional reports, and self-service query creation — all running live on transactional data with insight-to-action navigation into transactions. The 2025 release adds Fiori 4.0 touches: AI-assisted enterprise search, Joule integration, smart summarization, and AI-personalized My Home insight cards. Atlas v1 covers the essential core of the role-based home page, role dashboards, and tabular self-service reporting; it plans reduced subsets of the component library, floorplan patterns, semantic layer, KPI framework, and drill-down analytics; and it omits enterprise search, per-user personalization/variants, and AI-assisted UX entirely.
251	
252	| S/4HANA capability | Atlas v1 | Atlas module | Notes |
253	|---|---|---|---|
254	| **Role-based launchpad home with spaces/pages and app/KPI tiles** | Full | frontend | — |

Later: Grow the kit into a documented design system: theme tokens, a11y audit, and new controls added as app screens demand them. |

Later: Add a pivot/drill-down UI and chart rendering on top of existing report-builder queries. |

Later: Introduce a versioned semantic layer (named reusable views and measures) that the report builder, dashboards, and KPI tiles all consume. |
260	| **Smart Business KPI framework (Manage KPIs and Reports)** | Partial | reporting | Atlas ships a fixed set of KPI tiles and dashboard cards; end-user KPI authoring, threshold/target rules, color states, and publish-to-home are not planned. Later: Add a "manage KPIs" admin screen where a KPI = saved report query + threshold rules, publishable as a home-page tile. |
261	| **Self-service query creation and export (Query Browser, custom analytical queries)** | Full | reporting | — |
262	| **Insight-to-action and intent-based cross-app navigation** | Partial | frontend | Atlas plans a document-flow viewer component, but no generic deep-link/intent framework wiring dashboard cards and report rows to the owning app screens. Later: Define per-entity URL route conventions (deep links) and wire dashboard cards, KPI tiles, and report rows to them. |
263	| **Enterprise search across business objects** | Out of scope | — | Atlas v1 plans only per-report filters; no global cross-entity search or app finder exists anywhere in the plan. Later: Add a global search endpoint over key entities plus a header omnibox that deep-links into list/detail pages. |
264	| **Personalization and key-user UI adaptation** | Out of scope | — | Atlas v1 home pages, dashboards, and grids are role-defined and static; no per-user variants, tile rearrangement, or screen adaptation is planned. Later: Persist per-user grid/filter variants and home-tile layout as JSON preference records keyed by user and screen. |
265	| Joule and AI-assisted UX (NL navigation, smart summarization, easy filter) | Out of scope | — | Flagship 2025 differentiator but not yet baseline-essential, and largely premium/optional even in S/4HANA; nothing AI-related is in the Atlas v1 plan. Later: Once report-builder and search APIs exist, attach an LLM assistant that translates natural language into report definitions and deep links. |
266	
267	---
268	
269	## Industry Solutions approach
270	
271	SAP's S/4HANA industry approach folded most former IS add-ons into a single codebase ("industry to core"), covering roughly 25 industries whose functionality is activated per system through business function sets and the switch framework — activation is largely irreversible, one industry function set per instance, and industry-specific LoB functions are licensed separately from the Enterprise Management core. What the industry layer actually varies is substantial: terminology (Article vs Material, Site vs Plant), industry master data models (retail article/site, patient, equipment), entire vertical process suites (merchandise management, EC&O Equipment & Tools Management, professional-services Commercial Project Management, IS-U billing), regulatory content, and preconfigured SAP Best Practices content applied at setup. The current 2025/2026 direction adds a clean-core posture where deep vertical needs increasingly move to SAP Industry Cloud partner extensions on BTP — notably SAP is discontinuing healthcare IS-H by 2030 in favor of partner solutions. Atlas v1's YAML template layer maps well to the configuration-content slice of this area but plans none of the vertical process logic, industry master data objects, regulatory content, or partner extension ecosystem that practitioners associate with SAP industry solutions.
272	
273	| S/4HANA capability | Atlas v1 | Atlas module | Notes |
274	|---|---|---|---|
275	| **Single-core delivery with industry activation (business function sets / switch framework)** | Partial | industry | Atlas templates toggle modules and apply presets at tenant creation, but there is no deep switch layer that changes the behavior of shared module code per industry (e.g., retail switch altering core MM logistics flows). Later: Add a feature-flag/behavior-variant layer inside modules keyed off the tenant's industry template. |
276	| **Industry-specific terminology overrides** | Full | industry | — |
277	| **Industry-specific master data models** | Partial | industry | Typed custom fields (JSONB + metadata registry) extend core entities, but Atlas v1 plans no first-class industry entities such as article variant matrices, store hierarchies, or a patient demographics object. Later: Ship industry entities as optional modules built on the metadata registry, starting with retail article/site. |
278	| **Industry-specific end-to-end business processes** | Out of scope | — | Atlas v1 templates only configure existing horizontal modules; no industry-specific process logic of any kind is planned. Later: Post-v1 industry process packs as optional modules layered on core (e.g., a retail pack adding assortment/promotion flows). |
279	| **Preconfigured industry best-practice content applied at provisioning** | Full | industry | — |
280	| **Metadata-driven field extensibility surfaced across the UI** | Full | core | — |
281	| **Industry regulatory and statutory compliance** | Out of scope | — | Atlas v1 templates carry only default tax codes; no industry- or country-specific statutory logic, regulated billing, or POC revenue recognition is planned in the industry layer. Later: Country/industry compliance packs per module once a localization framework exists, prioritized by shipped templates. |
282	| **Breadth of industry coverage (~25 verticals)** | Partial | industry | Atlas v1 ships 5 templates (manufacturing, retail, professional-services, healthcare, construction); deep verticals like utilities, banking, or oil & gas need far more than configuration templates. Later: Grow template coverage via community-contributed YAML templates, pairing deep verticals with later process-pack modules. |
283	| **Partner and industry-cloud extension ecosystem** | Out of scope | — | Atlas v1 plans no plugin/extension API or marketplace through which third parties could ship industry functionality; templates are first-party YAML only. Later: Define a stable plugin API plus template packaging so third parties can publish installable industry packs. |
284	| **Lifecycle-safe industry configuration management** | Partial | industry | Idempotent template application at tenant creation is planned, but there is no template versioning or safe re-application/upgrade of templates to existing live tenants. Later: Version templates and add a migration-aware re-apply command that diffs template state against live tenant config. |

9	``code`` on the department and position. None claims a gapless document number — HR masters are not
10	posted documents in the D-012 sense (no docflow), unlike a maintenance order.
11	
12	THE SENSITIVE PERMISSION (D-009/D-052). ``hr.employee.read_compensation`` is the key the ``Masked``
13	serializer checks at serialization time: a viewer holding it sees the employee's compensation/PII
14	(salary, national/tax id, date of birth, bank account); a viewer without it sees those fields as
15	``None``. It is ALSO the gate on the dedicated compensation-WRITE endpoint (the masked fields are
16	excluded from the general Update; see ``schemas.py`` / ``router.py``). So a user may hold
17	``hr.employee.manage`` (edit name/department/etc.) yet NOT ``hr.employee.read_compensation`` — that
18	user manages employees but can neither see nor set their pay.
19	
20	SCOPE (s4hana-parity §HCM, D-052). v1 is employees + departments + positions + org chart. No
21	date-effective history, no formal hire/transfer/terminate actions, no leave, no timesheet, no real
22	payroll, no talent/recruiting/benefits.
23	"""
24	
25	from enum import StrEnum
26	
27	from app.core.rbac import register_permissions

30	class EmploymentStatus(StrEnum):
31	    """Lifecycle status of an EMPLOYEE (PLAN 10.1, D-052).
32	
33	    - **ACTIVE** — currently employed. The default at creation.
34	    - **ON_LEAVE** — temporarily away (parental, sabbatical, long absence) but still employed.
35	    - **TERMINATED** — employment ended. Terminal; ``termination_date`` is set. v1 has no formal
36	      terminate ACTION (date-effective actions are out of scope, D-052) — the status is set via the
37	      ordinary update path.
38	    """

40	    ACTIVE = "ACTIVE"
41	    ON_LEAVE = "ON_LEAVE"
42	    TERMINATED = "TERMINATED"

46	    """The employment ARRANGEMENT of an employee (PLAN 10.1, D-052).
47	
48	    - **FULL_TIME** — a permanent full-time employee. The default at creation.
49	    - **PART_TIME** — a permanent part-time employee.
50	    - **CONTRACT** — a fixed-term / contractor engagement.
51	    """
52	
53	    FULL_TIME = "FULL_TIME"
54	    PART_TIME = "PART_TIME"
55	    CONTRACT = "CONTRACT"
56	
57	
58	class LeaveRequestStatus(StrEnum):
59	    """Lifecycle of a LEAVE REQUEST (PLAN 10.2, D-053). The procurement requisition
60	    submit→approve→reject precedent (D-040), without a value-threshold rule — every request awaits
61	    a distinct ``hr.leave.approve`` holder.
62	
63	    - **DRAFT** — created, editable, not yet routed for approval. The default at creation.
64	    - **SUBMITTED** — filed for approval; awaits an approver. Editing is closed.
65	    - **APPROVED** — approved; the employee's leave balance for the type is DECREMENTED by the
66	      request days at this transition (the value-bearing step, D-053).
67	    - **REJECTED** — declined. Terminal; no balance effect.
68	    - **CANCELLED** — withdrawn. From DRAFT/SUBMITTED there is no balance effect; cancelling an
69	      APPROVED request RESTORES the decremented balance (D-053).
70	    """
71	
72	    DRAFT = "DRAFT"
73	    SUBMITTED = "SUBMITTED"
74	    APPROVED = "APPROVED"
75	    REJECTED = "REJECTED"
76	    CANCELLED = "CANCELLED"
77	
78	
79	class LeaveUnit(StrEnum):
80	    """The unit a leave type / request tracks in (PLAN 10.2, D-053). v1 tracks leave in **DAYS**
81	    only. Half-day granularity is expressible WITHOUT a new unit — ``days`` is a ``QuantityType``
82	    (NUMERIC scale 6, D-015), so a caller supplies ``0.5`` for a half day; a dedicated HALF_DAY unit
83	    (and shift-aware part-day math) is the documented later. The enum exists so the later unit set
84	    has a home and the column reads self-documenting."""
85	
86	    DAYS = "DAYS"
87

91	    ``accrual_amount`` on.
92	
93	    - **MONTHLY** — accrues each month (e.g. 1.67 days/month ≈ 20/year).
94	    - **ANNUAL** — accrues once per year (e.g. 20 days/year granted in one run).
95	
96	    The accrual run is invoked per frequency (``POST /leave-balances/accrue?frequency=``) so a
97	    tenant runs the monthly grant monthly and the annual grant yearly, each idempotent for its
98	    period (D-053).
99	    """
100	
101	    MONTHLY = "MONTHLY"
102	    ANNUAL = "ANNUAL"
103	
104	
105	# --- Permissions (D-009): one key per guarded endpoint action -----------------
106	# Employee + department + position masters each split read/manage. The employee adds the SENSITIVE
107	# read_compensation key (D-052): it gates BOTH the masked compensation/PII fields' visibility (the
108	# Masked serializer checks it) AND the dedicated compensation-write endpoint. A holder of
109	# hr.employee.manage can edit an employee's non-sensitive fields but, without read_compensation, can
110	# neither see nor write pay.
111	HR_EMPLOYEE_READ = "hr.employee.read"
112	HR_EMPLOYEE_MANAGE = "hr.employee.manage"
113	HR_EMPLOYEE_READ_COMPENSATION = "hr.employee.read_compensation"
114	HR_DEPARTMENT_READ = "hr.department.read"
115	HR_DEPARTMENT_MANAGE = "hr.department.manage"
116	HR_POSITION_READ = "hr.position.read"
117	HR_POSITION_MANAGE = "hr.position.manage"
118	
119	# Leave (PLAN 10.2, D-053). Leave TYPES are configuration (read/manage). A leave REQUEST splits the
120	# filing authority (``.request`` — an employee/manager files + submits + cancels their request) from
121	# the distinct APPROVAL authority (``.approve`` — the value-bearing decision that decrements the
122	# balance; the procurement requisition .approve precedent, D-040). The accrual RUN is gated by
123	# ``.manage`` on the leave type (running the grant is a configuration-owner action, no
124	# separate key —
125	# the maintenance .run precedent applies to time-based generation, but accrual is set-based over the
126	# type config, so the type-manage key suffices).
127	HR_LEAVE_TYPE_READ = "hr.leave_type.read"
128	HR_LEAVE_TYPE_MANAGE = "hr.leave_type.manage"
129	HR_LEAVE_READ = "hr.leave.read"

131	HR_LEAVE_APPROVE = "hr.leave.approve"

139	    HR_POSITION_READ,
140	    HR_POSITION_MANAGE,
141	    HR_LEAVE_TYPE_READ,
142	    HR_LEAVE_TYPE_MANAGE,
143	    HR_LEAVE_READ,
144	    HR_LEAVE_REQUEST,
145	    HR_LEAVE_APPROVE,
146	    descriptions={
147	        HR_EMPLOYEE_READ: "Read employees (compensation/PII masked)",
148	        HR_EMPLOYEE_MANAGE: "Create and edit employees (non-compensation fields)",
149	        HR_EMPLOYEE_READ_COMPENSATION: "View and set employee compensation and PII",
150	        HR_DEPARTMENT_READ: "Read departments",
151	        HR_DEPARTMENT_MANAGE: "Create and edit departments",
152	        HR_POSITION_READ: "Read positions",
153	        HR_POSITION_MANAGE: "Create and edit positions",
154	        HR_LEAVE_TYPE_READ: "Read leave types",

156	        HR_LEAVE_READ: "Read leave requests and balances",
157	        HR_LEAVE_REQUEST: "File, submit and cancel leave requests",
158	        HR_LEAVE_APPROVE: "Approve or reject leave requests",

content.content:
272	## D-015 — Money and quantity representation (exact on both engines)
273	
274	**Decision.**
275	Three TypeDecorators in `core/models.py`: `MoneyType`, `QuantityType` (PG NUMERIC(18,6); SQLite INTEGER storing Decimal × 10^6 micro-units) and `RateType` (PG NUMERIC(20,10); SQLite INTEGER × 10^10), converting to/from `decimal.Decimal` in `process_bind_param`/`process_result_value`. This explicitly supersedes D-003's "plain Numeric" wording: SQLAlchemy's `Numeric` on SQLite round-trips through float and silently loses precision, which would make the exact-sum DB triggers and tests nondeterministic.
276	
277	- **Aggregations** always go through SQLAlchemy Core expressions (`func.sum(JournalLine.functional_debit_amount)`) so the argument's type propagates and result conversion applies on both backends; raw textual SQL against money columns is banned in `app/` (grep gate; tests exempt).
278	- **Python:** only `Decimal` represents money/quantities; Pydantic v2 schemas declare `Decimal` fields, JSON-serializing as strings (Pydantic JSON-mode default); the frontend types money as `string` and formats exclusively in `lib/format.ts`.
279	- **Rounding:** amounts quantize at the posting/pricing boundary to the currency's decimal_places from `fin_currencies` (ISO 4217: JPY=0, USD=2, BHD=3) via `Decimal.quantize(ROUND_HALF_UP)`; stored journal amounts never carry sub-minor-unit digits despite scale-6 headroom; unit prices/costs and FX rates keep full scale.
280	- **Allocation:** a single `allocate(total, weights) -> list[Decimal]` largest-remainder helper plus quantize helpers live in `core/money.py` — a new flat core file recorded in DECISIONS.md as a STRUCTURE §2 amendment (one file per cross-cutting concern) — used by tax splits, payment allocation, cost allocations, AND functional-currency balancing in journal posting, so parts always sum exactly to totals everywhere.
281	- **Quantities** use scale 6 for UoM/FIFO math; display precision is frontend-only.
282	- **Trigger discipline:** hand-written trigger SQL performs only comparisons and SUMs on the stored representation (integers on SQLite, NUMERIC on PG) — never division or scaling — so the asymmetric storage stays semantically identical where it matters.
283	
284	**Rationale.**
285	The financial engine's DB-level invariants (balance trigger, one-side CHECK, valuation math) are only meaningful if storage is exact on BOTH backends; integer micro-units are the standard exact representation where a true decimal type is absent. ROUND_HALF_UP matches commercial/SAP practice on user-facing documents. Centralizing largest-remainder in `core/money.py` guarantees the journal's functional-balance mechanism and every split use the same arithmetic — the drafts had it in two places with slightly different semantics.
286	
287	**Rejected alternatives.**
288	- Plain `sa.Numeric` everywhere: float round-trips on SQLite break exact trigger sums.
289	- TEXT decimals on SQLite: `SUM()` over TEXT does float math.
290	- ROUND_HALF_EVEN: statistically nicer, but surprises users reconciling invoices/tax and diverges from commercial practice.
291	- Integer minor units on Postgres too: NUMERIC is native, exact, and keeps psql/BI-friendly raw SQL.
292	
293	**Risks & mitigations.**
294	- Dialect-asymmetric storage means per-dialect trigger SQL — bounded by the comparison-and-SUM-only rule and bypass tests on both backends.
295	- SQLite int64 caps amounts around 9.2e12 currency units at scale 6 — ample for demo/tests; PG runtime has full NUMERIC range.
296	- A future trigger needing arithmetic beyond SUM must be written per-dialect with explicit review.
297	
298	---
299	
300	## D-016 — Custom fields: core-owned JSONB + metadata registry (ownership fixed)
301	
302	**Decision.**
303	**Ownership fix:** the draft put the registry and validator in `modules/industry`, which forces finance/inventory/hr services to import industry — an upward dependency violating STRUCTURE §5 (finance is the bottom of the import order); the parity doc itself assigns "metadata-driven field extensibility" to core. Therefore:
304	
305	**Registry table `core_custom_field_defs`** (id, tenant_id, entity_key like `'inventory.item'`, field_key validated by `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,49}$`, label, field_type enum TEXT|NUMBER|DECIMAL|BOOLEAN|DATE|SELECT, is_required, options JSON for SELECT, validation JSON `{min,max,regex,max_length}`, display_group, display_order, is_active; UNIQUE(tenant_id, entity_key, field_key)) and its logic live in `core/custom_fields.py` — a new flat core file recorded in DECISIONS.md as a STRUCTURE §2 amendment.
306	
307	It exposes:
308	
309	- `custom_fields_column()` returning `MutableDict.as_mutable(sa.JSON(none_as_null=False).with_variant(postgresql.JSONB(), 'postgresql'))`, NOT NULL server_default `'{}'`, applied by every extensible entity (item, vendor, customer, journal-entry header, sales/purchase docs, employee, equipment);
310	- `validate_custom_fields(session, tenant_id, entity_key, payload) -> dict`, called by owning-module services on create/update: loads active defs (per-request cached), rejects unknown keys, enforces required-on-create, coerces per type — DATE as ISO-8601 string, DECIMAL as string parsed via `Decimal` (never JSON float, consistent with D-015), NUMBER int, BOOLEAN bool, SELECT membership.
311	
312	Defs are WRITTEN by industry-template application at provisioning and by an admin CRUD endpoint (`/api/v1/admin/custom-field-defs`) — both call core service functions, keeping data ownership at the platform level while templates supply content. Pydantic schemas type the field `custom_fields: dict[str, Any] = {}`; the service validator is the gate.
313	
314	**Report builder** reads defs via core and builds portable expressions with `Model.custom_fields['key'].as_string()/.as_integer()/.as_boolean()` (renders `->>` on PG, `JSON_EXTRACT` on SQLite); DECIMAL sort/aggregation casts through Numeric on PG; on SQLite uses CAST to REAL and is documented display-grade. Keys are flat top-level scalars only (registry enforces no nesting). Optional Postgres-only GIN indexes ship in dialect-branched Alembic migrations when a template declares searchable fields; the SQLite arm is a no-op.
315	
316	**Rationale.**
317	One nullable-free JSON column per entity keeps migrations trivial when templates add fields; routing validation through the owning service preserves service-layer-owns-logic; and moving the registry to core resolves the dependency inversion cleanly — modules import core freely, so every module can validate without touching industry. The portable JSON path API confines all PG/SQLite JSON divergence to two call sites.
318	
319	**Rejected alternatives.**
320	- Industry-module ownership (the draft): upward imports from finance/inventory — a hard STRUCTURE violation; rejected outright rather than "interpreted around".
321	- EAV table: row explosion, painful reports.
322	- Per-field ALTER TABLE: per-tenant DDL is operationally dangerous and unexpressible in linear Alembic history.
323	- Dynamic per-tenant Pydantic models: runtime model building for zero gain over a dict validator.
324	- DECIMAL values as JSON numbers: floats by another name.
325	
326	**Risks & mitigations.**
327	- Custom fields are invisible to DB constraints — accepted: they are descriptive/reporting fields by design; anything participating in financial invariants must be a real column (rule recorded in `docs/modules/industry.md`).
328	- Field deactivation orphans stored values — `is_active` soft-deactivation only, never hard delete.
329	- `JSON_EXTRACT` vs `->>` nested-value divergence — moot under the flat-scalar restriction.
330	
331	---
332	
333	## D-017 — Universal journal schema, posting protocol, and reversal
334	
335	**Decision.**
336	`modules/finance/models.py`.
337	
338	**Header `fin_journal_entries`:** id `sa.Uuid` app-generated, tenant_id, entry_number text NULLABLE with partial unique index (tenant_id, entry_number) WHERE entry_number IS NOT NULL — FIXED from the draft's NOT NULL: numbers are claimed at POSTING per the D-012 claim-timing rule so abandoned drafts cannot burn gapless numbers; document_type enum (MANUAL, AP_INVOICE, AR_INVOICE, PAYMENT, COGS, FX_REVAL, DEPRECIATION, REVERSAL, …), status DRAFT|POSTED|REVERSED, posting_date, fiscal_period_id FK, currency_code (one transaction currency per entry; cross-currency events become multiple entries), functional_currency_code, exchange_rate RateType, description, posted_at, posted_by_user_id, reversal_of_entry_id self-FK UNIQUE, reversed_by_entry_id self-FK, DocumentMixin document_id. REMOVED from the draft: the header idempotency_key column — idempotency has exactly one home, `core_idempotency_keys` (two uncoordinated mechanisms invite divergence).
339	
340	**Lines `fin_journal_lines`:** id, tenant_id, entry_id FK, line_number (UNIQUE(entry_id, line_number)), account_id NOT NULL, nullable dimension FKs on every line (cost_center_id, profit_center_id, wbs_element_id, item_id, vendor_id, customer_id as typed FKs, warehouse_id, tax_code_id), quantity QuantityType + uom_code, MoneyType amount pairs debit_amount/credit_amount (transaction) and functional_debit_amount/functional_credit_amount, all NOT NULL DEFAULT 0; denormalized posting_date, fiscal_period_id, is_posted for projections.
341	
342	**DDL:** named CHECK `ck_fin_journal_lines_one_side`: `(debit_amount > 0 AND credit_amount = 0) OR (credit_amount > 0 AND debit_amount = 0)`; companion CHECK that functional amounts are non-negative, not both positive, and on the same side as the transaction side (functional zero allowed).
343	
344	**Functional balance fix:** the draft's separate rounding-difference line is impossible — a functional-only line has zero transaction amounts and violates the mandated one-side CHECK — so the residual functional cent from translation is absorbed into the largest line's functional amount via `core/money.py` `allocate()` (largest-remainder), making functional sums balance with no special lines.
345	
346	**Balance backstop:** per-dialect trigger on `fin_journal_entries` firing on the DRAFT→POSTED UPDATE, SUM-checking debits == credits over the entry's lines in BOTH currency pairs, raising `ATLAS_UNBALANCED_ENTRY` (plpgsql RAISE / SQLite `RAISE(ABORT)`) — exact on both engines per D-015.

1	"""HR leave models (PLAN 10.2, parity HCM "Leave and absence management" = Full): the ``LeaveType``
2	configuration, the running ``LeaveBalance`` per employee per type, and the ``LeaveRequest`` doc.
3	
4	THREE tables, one concern (leave), the D-053 model:
5	
6	- ``LeaveType`` is a MASTER keyed by a USER-SUPPLIED ``code`` unique per tenant (the item-code /
7	  leave-config precedent — no gapless number, no DocumentMixin). It defines the accrual cadence
8	  (``accrual_frequency``), the per-period grant (``accrual_amount``, a ``QuantityType`` so
9	  1.67/month is exact, D-015), an optional accrual cap (``max_balance``), whether the leave is paid,
10	  and active.
11	- ``LeaveBalance`` is the RUNNING balance per (employee, type): ``balance_days`` available now,
12	  ``accrued_to_date`` and ``taken_to_date`` for traceability, and ``last_accrual_period`` — the
13	  idempotency guard the accrual run keys off (a YYYY-MM / YYYY string; the run skips a balance whose
14	  ``last_accrual_period`` already equals the run's period, so a re-run grants nothing — the
15	  maintenance next-due-date idempotency analogue, set-based, D-053). UNIQUE(tenant, employee, type).
16	- ``LeaveRequest`` is the request DOCUMENT: it claims a gapless ``LV-`` ``request_number`` at
17	  creation (D-040 claim-at-create precedent) but is NOT a docflow document (no DocumentMixin — a
18	  leave request has no successor document in v1). ``days`` is caller-supplied (a ``QuantityType``
19	  validated > 0; ``start_date``/``end_date`` are stored for reference, ``end >= start`` enforced in
20	  the service — calendar/business-day computation from the dates is the documented later, D-053).
21	  ``status`` runs the lifecycle; ``approved_by`` / ``decided_at`` capture the decision.
22	
23	ALL THREE are composite-tenant-FK'd to their parents (employee, leave type), so a child can never
24	point at a parent of another tenant. ``approved_by`` is an OPAQUE core users id (the deciding
25	user — nullable, no hard FK to core_users, the ``Employee.user_id`` precedent, D-029).
26	"""
27	
28	import uuid
29	from datetime import date, datetime
30	from decimal import Decimal
31

33	from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column

36	    AuditMixin,
37	    Base,

47	    LeaveRequestStatus,

52	class LeaveType(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, AuditMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
53	    """A LEAVE TYPE (D-053): the configuration of one kind of leave (annual, sick, …).
54	
55	    ``code`` is USER-SUPPLIED and unique per tenant. ``accrual_frequency`` (AccrualFrequency) and
56	    ``accrual_amount`` (QuantityType — days per period) drive the accrual run; ``max_balance``
57	    (QuantityType, nullable) caps the accrued balance (None = uncapped). ``unit`` is the tracking
58	    unit (DAYS in v1). ``is_paid`` flags paid leave; ``is_active`` flags a retired type the accrual
59	    run skips. Audited (D-010): leave config drives balances.

62	    __tablename__ = "hr_leave_types"

64	        sa.UniqueConstraint("tenant_id", "code", name="uq_hr_leave_types_tenant_id_code"),

78	    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(200), nullable=False)
79	    accrual_frequency: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(

87	    unit: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(

92	    )

98	class LeaveBalance(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
99	    """The RUNNING leave balance per (employee, leave type) (D-053).
100	
101	    Composite tenant FKs to ``hr_employees`` and ``hr_leave_types``. UNIQUE(tenant, employee, type)
102	    — one balance row per pairing. ``balance_days`` (QuantityType) is the currently available amount
103	    the approve step decrements and a cancel-of-approved restores; ``accrued_to_date`` /
104	    ``taken_to_date`` are running totals for traceability. ``last_accrual_period`` is the
105	    IDEMPOTENCY GUARD: the accrual run stamps it with the run's period (YYYY-MM for MONTHLY, YYYY
106	    for ANNUAL)
107	    and skips any balance already stamped with the current period, so a same-period re-run grants
108	    nothing (D-053). NOT audited (a high-churn running total, the stock-balance precedent).
109	    """

111	    __tablename__ = "hr_leave_balances"
112	    __table_args__ = (
113	        sa.UniqueConstraint(
114	            "tenant_id",

10	bounded by ``MAX_HIERARCHY_DEPTH`` (D-052) and the org-chart build issues ONE query for all
11	employees (PERFORMANCE §6: a bounded recursive read in memory, no per-node N+1).

71	async def employee_manager_chain(
72	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, employee_id: uuid.UUID
73	) -> list[Employee]:
74	    """The reporting chain from ``employee_id`` UP to the top (D-052): [self, manager, manager's
75	    manager, ...]. Bounded by ``MAX_HIERARCHY_DEPTH`` so a malformed chain (should be impossible
76	    given the service cycle guard) cannot spin forever. Empty if the employee does not exist."""
77	    chain: list[Employee] = []
78	    seen: set[uuid.UUID] = set()
79	    current_id: uuid.UUID | None = employee_id
80	    for _ in range(MAX_HIERARCHY_DEPTH):
81	        if current_id is None or current_id in seen:
82	            break
83	        current = await get_employee(session, tenant_id, current_id)
84	        if current is None:
85	            break
86	        chain.append(current)
87	        seen.add(current.id)
88	        current_id = current.manager_id
89	    return chain

92	async def org_chart_for(
93	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, root_employee_id: uuid.UUID | None = None
94	) -> tuple[list[Employee], dict[uuid.UUID, list[Employee]]]:
95	    """The data for the reporting org chart (D-052), as (roots, children-by-manager-id).
96	
97	    ONE query loads every employee in the tenant (PERFORMANCE §6: no per-node N+1); the tree is
98	    built
99	    in memory. ``roots`` are the top of the chart — the employee with ``root_employee_id`` when
100	    given
101	    (a sub-tree anchored on one manager), else every employee with no manager. ``children`` maps a
102	    manager id to its direct reports (each list ordered by employee_code, matching the query order).
103	    The service walks this bounded by ``MAX_HIERARCHY_DEPTH`` to assemble the nested nodes.
104	    """
105	    stmt = select(Employee).where(Employee.tenant_id == tenant_id).order_by(Employee.employee_code)
106	    employees = list((await session.execute(stmt)).scalars().all())
107	    children: dict[uuid.UUID, list[Employee]] = {}
108	    for employee in employees:
109	        if employee.manager_id is not None:
110	            children.setdefault(employee.manager_id, []).append(employee)
111	    if root_employee_id is not None:
112	        roots = [e for e in employees if e.id == root_employee_id]
113	    else:
114	        roots = [e for e in employees if e.manager_id is None]
115	    return roots, children

1	"""Leave-request lifecycle (PLAN 10.2, D-053): create → submit → approve/reject → cancel, with the
2	balance decrement on approve and restore on cancel-of-approved.
3	
4	The service layer owns every rule (CLAUDE.md rule 7); the router stays thin. The request lifecycle
5	mirrors the procurement requisition submit→approve→reject precedent (D-040), without a value
6	threshold — every SUBMITTED request awaits a distinct ``hr.leave.approve`` holder. Leave-TYPE CRUD
7	and balance reads live in ``leave_config.py``; the accrual run in ``leave_accrual.py``.
8	
9	THE BALANCE EFFECT (the headline of 10.2, D-053):
10	- APPROVE decrements the employee's balance for the type by ``days`` (raising ``taken_to_date``). If
11	  the balance is insufficient → 422 ``hr.insufficient_leave_balance`` (v1 BLOCKS negative balances;
12	  an allow-negative leave type is the documented later). A missing balance row counts as 0
13	  available.
14	- CANCEL of an APPROVED request RESTORES the balance (adds ``days`` back, lowers ``taken_to_date``);
15	  cancel from DRAFT/SUBMITTED has no balance effect.
16	
17	``from __future__ import annotations`` keeps ``Page[...]`` of the ORM models a string at import.
18	"""
19	
20	from __future__ import annotations
21	
22	import uuid
23	from datetime import UTC, date, datetime
24	from decimal import Decimal
25	
26	from sqlalchemy import select
27	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
28	
29	from app.core.exceptions import ConflictError, NotFoundError, ValidationFailedError
30	from app.core.numbering import claim_number, ensure_sequence
31	from app.core.pagination import DEFAULT_LIMIT, OrderKey, SortDirection, filter_fingerprint, paginate
32	from app.core.schemas import Page
33	from app.modules.hr import queries as hr_queries
34	from app.modules.hr.constants import (
35	    LEAVE_REQUEST_NUMBER_PADDING,
36	    LEAVE_REQUEST_NUMBER_PREFIX,
37	    LEAVE_REQUEST_SEQUENCE_NAME,
38	    LeaveRequestStatus,
39	)
40	from app.modules.hr.models import LeaveBalance, LeaveRequest
41	from app.modules.hr.schemas import (
42	    LeaveRequestCreate,
43	    LeaveRequestFilter,
44	    LeaveRequestUpdate,
45	)
46	from app.modules.hr.service.leave_config import get_leave_type
47	
48	# --- Leave request lifecycle --------------------------------------------------
49	
50	
51	async def get_leave_request(
52	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, request_id: uuid.UUID
53	) -> LeaveRequest:
54	    request = await session.get(LeaveRequest, request_id)
55	    if request is None or request.tenant_id != tenant_id:
56	        raise NotFoundError(message="Leave request not found", code="hr.leave_request_not_found")
57	    return request
58	
59	
60	def _validate_request_dates(start_date: date, end_date: date, days: Decimal) -> None:
61	    if end_date < start_date:
62	        raise ValidationFailedError(
63	            message="The end date cannot be before the start date",
64	            code="hr.leave_dates_invalid",
65	            details={"start_date": str(start_date), "end_date": str(end_date)},
66	        )
67	    if days <= 0:
68	        raise ValidationFailedError(
69	            message="Leave days must be greater than zero",
70	            code="hr.leave_days_invalid",
71	            details={"days": str(days)},
72	        )
73	
74	
75	async def create_leave_request(
76	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, payload: LeaveRequestCreate
77	) -> LeaveRequest:
78	    """Create a DRAFT leave request (D-053). Validates the employee + leave type exist, days > 0 and
79	    end >= start; claims a gapless ``LV-`` number at creation (D-040 precedent). No balance effect
80	    until approve."""
81	    if not await hr_queries.employee_exists(session, tenant_id, payload.employee_id):
82	        raise ValidationFailedError(
83	            message="Referenced employee does not exist",
84	            code="hr.employee_not_found",
85	            details={"employee_id": str(payload.employee_id)},
86	        )
87	    # Validate the leave type exists (load raises a clean 404-shaped error if not).
88	    await get_leave_type(session, tenant_id, payload.leave_type_id)
89	    _validate_request_dates(payload.start_date, payload.end_date, payload.days)
90	
91	    await ensure_sequence(
92	        session,
93	        tenant_id,
94	        LEAVE_REQUEST_SEQUENCE_NAME,
95	        LEAVE_REQUEST_NUMBER_PREFIX,
96	        LEAVE_REQUEST_NUMBER_PADDING,
97	        year_reset=True,
98	    )
99	    number = await claim_number(
100	        session, tenant_id, LEAVE_REQUEST_SEQUENCE_NAME, on_date=payload.start_date
101	    )
102	    request = LeaveRequest(
103	        tenant_id=tenant_id,
104	        request_number=number,
105	        employee_id=payload.employee_id,
106	        leave_type_id=payload.leave_type_id,
107	        start_date=payload.start_date,
108	        end_date=payload.end_date,
109	        days=payload.days,
110	        status=LeaveRequestStatus.DRAFT.value,
111	        reason=payload.reason,
112	        notes=payload.notes,
113	    )
114	    session.add(request)
115	    await session.flush()
116	    return request
117	
118	
119	async def update_leave_request(
120	    session: AsyncSession,
121	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
122	    request_id: uuid.UUID,
123	    payload: LeaveRequestUpdate,
124	) -> LeaveRequest:
125	    """Partial update of a DRAFT leave request (D-053). Only a DRAFT is editable; ``employee_id`` /
126	    ``leave_type_id`` are immutable. The resulting date range / days is re-validated."""
127	    request = await get_leave_request(session, tenant_id, request_id)
128	    if LeaveRequestStatus(request.status) != LeaveRequestStatus.DRAFT:
129	        raise ConflictError(
130	            message="Only a draft leave request can be edited",
131	            code="hr.leave_request_not_draft",
132	            details={"status": request.status},
133	        )
134	    data = payload.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
135	    for field, value in data.items():
136	        setattr(request, field, value)
137	    _validate_request_dates(request.start_date, request.end_date, request.days)
138	    await session.flush()
139	    return request
140	
141	
142	async def submit_leave_request(
143	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, request_id: uuid.UUID
144	) -> LeaveRequest:
145	    """Submit a DRAFT leave request (D-053): DRAFT → SUBMITTED, awaiting an approver. Re-submitting
146	    a non-draft is a conflict."""
147	    request = await get_leave_request(session, tenant_id, request_id)
148	    if LeaveRequestStatus(request.status) != LeaveRequestStatus.DRAFT:
149	        raise ConflictError(
150	            message="Only a draft leave request can be submitted",
151	            code="hr.leave_request_not_draft",
152	            details={"status": request.status},
153	        )
154	    request.status = LeaveRequestStatus.SUBMITTED.value
155	    await session.flush()
156	    return request
157	
158	
159	async def _balance_for_update(
160	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, employee_id: uuid.UUID, leave_type_id: uuid.UUID
161	) -> LeaveBalance | None:
162	    return await hr_queries.get_leave_balance(session, tenant_id, employee_id, leave_type_id)
163	
164	
165	async def approve_leave_request(
166	    session: AsyncSession,
167	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
168	    request_id: uuid.UUID,
169	    *,
170	    approved_by: uuid.UUID,
171	    notes: str | None = None,
172	) -> LeaveRequest:
173	    """Approve a SUBMITTED leave request (D-053, the ``hr.leave.approve`` action). DECREMENTS the
174	    employee's balance for the type by ``days`` (raising ``taken_to_date``); if the available
175	    balance is below ``days`` → 422 ``hr.insufficient_leave_balance`` (v1 blocks negative balances).
176	    A missing balance row counts as 0 available. Records the approver + decision time."""
177	    request = await get_leave_request(session, tenant_id, request_id)
178	    if LeaveRequestStatus(request.status) != LeaveRequestStatus.SUBMITTED:
179	        raise ConflictError(
180	            message="Only a submitted leave request can be approved",
181	            code="hr.leave_request_not_submitted",
182	            details={"status": request.status},
183	        )
184	    balance = await _balance_for_update(
185	        session, tenant_id, request.employee_id, request.leave_type_id
186	    )
187	    available = balance.balance_days if balance is not None else Decimal(0)
188	    if available < request.days:
189	        raise ValidationFailedError(
190	            message="Insufficient leave balance for this request",
191	            code="hr.insufficient_leave_balance",
192	            details={"available": str(available), "requested": str(request.days)},
193	        )
194	    balance.balance_days -= request.days
195	    balance.taken_to_date += request.days
196	    request.status = LeaveRequestStatus.APPROVED.value
197	    request.approved_by = approved_by
198	    request.decided_at = datetime.now(UTC)
199	    request.notes = notes if notes is not None else request.notes
200	    await session.flush()
201	    return request
202	
203	
204	async def reject_leave_request(
205	    session: AsyncSession,
206	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
207	    request_id: uuid.UUID,
208	    *,
209	    approved_by: uuid.UUID,
210	    notes: str | None = None,
211	) -> LeaveRequest:
212	    """Reject a SUBMITTED leave request (D-053): SUBMITTED → REJECTED. No balance effect. Records
213	    the decider + decision time."""
214	    request = await get_leave_request(session, tenant_id, request_id)
215	    if LeaveRequestStatus(request.status) != LeaveRequestStatus.SUBMITTED:
216	        raise ConflictError(
217	            message="Only a submitted leave request can be rejected",
218	            code="hr.leave_request_not_submitted",
219	            details={"status": request.status},
220	        )
221	    request.status = LeaveRequestStatus.REJECTED.value
222	    request.approved_by = approved_by
223	    request.decided_at = datetime.now(UTC)
224	    request.notes = notes if notes is not None else request.notes
225	    await session.flush()
226	    return request
227	
228	
229	async def cancel_leave_request(
230	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, request_id: uuid.UUID
231	) -> LeaveRequest:
232	    """Cancel a leave request (D-053). Allowed from DRAFT/SUBMITTED (no balance effect) or APPROVED
233	    (RESTORES the balance: adds ``days`` back, lowers ``taken_to_date``). A terminal request
234	    (REJECTED/CANCELLED) cannot be cancelled."""
235	    request = await get_leave_request(session, tenant_id, request_id)
236	    status = LeaveRequestStatus(request.status)

244	        balance = await _balance_for_update(

246	        )
247	        if balance is not None:

249	            balance.taken_to_date -= request.days

3	Split out of ``leave.py`` so each leave file stays under the 400-line cap (the request lifecycle is
4	the busier concern). The leave TYPE is the configuration the accrual run and a request reference;
5	``get_leave_type`` is reused by the request-create validation in ``leave.py``. Leave BALANCES are
6	read-only over the API — they are written by the accrual run (``leave_accrual.py``) and the request
7	approve/cancel transitions (``leave.py``).
8	
9	``from __future__ import annotations`` keeps ``Page[LeaveType]`` a string at import.
10	"""

12	from __future__ import annotations
13

28	def _validate_accrual(accrual_amount: Decimal, max_balance: Decimal | None) -> None:
29	    """The leave-type accrual invariants (D-053): ``accrual_amount`` >= 0, and when a cap is set it
30	    must be >= ``accrual_amount`` (a cap below one period's grant would make every accrual a no-op —
31	    a misconfiguration, rejected)."""
32	    if accrual_amount < 0:
33	        raise ValidationFailedError(
34	            message="Accrual amount cannot be negative",
35	            code="hr.leave_accrual_invalid",
36	            details={"accrual_amount": str(accrual_amount)},
37	        )
38	    if max_balance is not None and max_balance < accrual_amount:
39	        raise ValidationFailedError(
40	            message="Maximum balance cannot be below the accrual amount",
41	            code="hr.leave_max_balance_invalid",
42	            details={"max_balance": str(max_balance), "accrual_amount": str(accrual_amount)},
43	        )

46	async def get_leave_type(
47	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, leave_type_id: uuid.UUID
48	) -> LeaveType:
49	    leave_type = await session.get(LeaveType, leave_type_id)
50	    if leave_type is None or leave_type.tenant_id != tenant_id:
51	        raise NotFoundError(message="Leave type not found", code="hr.leave_type_not_found")

55	async def create_leave_type(
56	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, payload: LeaveTypeCreate
57	) -> LeaveType:
58	    """Create a leave type. Rejects a duplicate code; validates the accrual invariants."""
59	    existing = (
60	        await session.execute(
61	            select(LeaveType.id).where(
62	                LeaveType.tenant_id == tenant_id, LeaveType.code == payload.code
63	            )
64	        )
65	    ).first()
66	    if existing is not None:
67	        raise ConflictError(
68	            message=f"Leave type with code {payload.code} already exists",
69	            code="hr.leave_type_code_conflict",
70	            details={"code": payload.code},
71	        )
72	    _validate_accrual(payload.accrual_amount, payload.max_balance)
73	    leave_type = LeaveType(
74	        tenant_id=tenant_id,
75	        code=payload.code,
76	        name=payload.name,
77	        accrual_frequency=payload.accrual_frequency,
78	        accrual_amount=payload.accrual_amount,
79	        max_balance=payload.max_balance,
80	        unit=payload.unit,
81	        is_paid=payload.is_paid,
82	        is_active=payload.is_active,
83	    )
84	    session.add(leave_type)
85	    await session.flush()

89	async def update_leave_type(
90	    session: AsyncSession,
91	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
92	    leave_type_id: uuid.UUID,
93	    payload: LeaveTypeUpdate,
94	) -> LeaveType:

96	    accrual amount / cap is re-validated against the resulting pair."""
97	    leave_type = await get_leave_type(session, tenant_id, leave_type_id)
98	    data = payload.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
99	    new_amount = data.get("accrual_amount", leave_type.accrual_amount)
100	    new_cap = data.get("max_balance", leave_type.max_balance)
101	    if "accrual_amount" in data or "max_balance" in data:
102	        _validate_accrual(new_amount, new_cap)
103	    for field, value in data.items():

1	"""HR org masters (PLAN 10.1, parity HCM core = employees + departments + positions + org chart):
2	the ``Department``, ``Position`` and ``Employee`` masters.
3	
4	THREE tables, one concern (the HCM org core). The hr models became a PACKAGE in PLAN 10.2 (leave
5	landed in a sibling ``leave.py``); this file holds the org masters unchanged.
6	
7	All three are MASTERS keyed by a USER-SUPPLIED ``code`` unique per tenant (the item-code / work-
8	centre precedent — no gapless document number, no DocumentMixin: HR masters are not posted documents
9	in the D-012 sense).
10	
11	THE DEPARTMENT↔MANAGER CIRCULAR REFERENCE (D-052). A department has a manager EMPLOYEE; an employee
12	belongs to a department — a hard composite FK each way would be a circular table dependency the
13	migration could not order. Resolution: ``Department.manager_employee_id`` is a PLAIN nullable
14	``sa.Uuid`` (opaque, validated in the service against ``hr_employees``), NOT a composite FK; the
15	employee→department side IS a real composite FK. So the dependency is one-directional at the DDL
16	level (employee → department), and the manager link is a service-validated soft reference. The
17	EMPLOYEE's org-chart reporting line (``manager_id``) and the DEPARTMENT hierarchy (``parent_id``)
18	are intra-table SELF composite FKs (a child can never point at a parent of another tenant); the
19	service
20	guards both against cycles with a bounded walk-up.
21	
22	CROSS-MODULE / SOFT IDS ARE OPAQUE (D-029/§5). ``Department.cost_center_id`` is an OPAQUE finance
23	cost-centre id (nullable, validated via finance/queries when set — never a cross-module FK).
24	``Employee.user_id`` is an OPAQUE core users id (nullable, validated via a core user probe when
25	set — an employee MAY also be a system user; never a hard FK from a module table to core_users).
26	
27	THE MASKED FIELDS (D-009/D-052) live on ``Employee`` as ordinary columns — ``base_salary``
28	(MoneyType), ``currency_code``, ``national_id``, ``tax_id``, ``date_of_birth``, ``bank_account``.
29	The
30	masking is a READ-side concern of the schema layer (the ``Masked`` serializer), not the model; the
31	columns store the real values. They are excluded from the audit diff (D-010) — compensation/PII is
32	captured in v1 only through the same masking machinery in the audit viewer (a documented later); for
33	now ``__audit_exclude__`` keeps the raw values out of the diff rows entirely, matching the
34	password_hash precedent on User.
35	"""
36	
37	import uuid
38	from datetime import date
39	from decimal import Decimal
40	
41	import sqlalchemy as sa
42	from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column
43	
44	from app.core.models import (
45	    AuditMixin,
46	    Base,
47	    TenantMixin,
48	    TimestampMixin,
49	    UuidPKMixin,
50	    tenant_fk,
51	    tenant_unique,
52	)
53	from app.core.money import MoneyType
54	from app.modules.hr.constants import EmploymentStatus, EmploymentType
55	
56	
57	class Department(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, AuditMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
58	    """An organizational DEPARTMENT (D-052): a unit employees and positions belong to.
59	
60	    ``code`` is USER-SUPPLIED and unique per tenant. ``parent_id`` (nullable) is the self composite
61	    tenant FK forming the department HIERARCHY (a sub-department's parent); the service guards it
62	    against cycles. ``cost_center_id`` is an OPAQUE finance cost-centre id (nullable, validated via
63	    finance/queries when set — D-029, no cross-module FK) for labour-cost attribution.
64	    ``manager_employee_id`` is the department's manager EMPLOYEE — a PLAIN nullable ``sa.Uuid``
65	    (opaque, validated in the service against ``hr_employees``), NOT a composite FK, to break the
66	    department↔employee circular table dependency (D-052; see module docstring). ``is_active`` flags
67	    a retired department. Audited (D-010): master data driving the org structure.
68	    """
69	
70	    __tablename__ = "hr_departments"
71	    __table_args__ = (
72	        sa.UniqueConstraint("tenant_id", "code", name="uq_hr_departments_tenant_id_code"),
73	        tenant_unique(),
74	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
